description: The governance register of related parties: who is related to this company, in what capacity, from when, and which document says so. This is not the transactional Party field on a Journal Entry — that stays Supplier / Customer / Employee. This answers the disclosure question instead: at 1099 time, at audit time, and on the related-party schedule of a return.

fields.description: The party's legal name, as it appears on the document that establishes the relationship. The docname is built from this and the company's abbreviation.
fields.label: Party Name
Party Type
fields.options:
Individual
Trust
LLC
Corporation
Partnership
Family Member
Other

fields.description: What the party DOES here. A person can hold two roles — a Manager who is also a Member — which is two entries, because the documents that govern them are different documents.
fields.label: Relationship to Company
fields.options:
Member
Manager
Trustee
Beneficiary
Family
Vendor
Officer
Director
Other

fields.description: When the relationship started — the date on the operating agreement, the trust instrument, the appointment.
fields.label: Effective Date

fields.description: When it ended. Empty means current. An ended relationship is never deleted: the transactions it explains are still in the ledger.
fields.label: End Date

fields.description: The LAST FOUR DIGITS ONLY. A full SSN or EIN must not be stored here — this field exists so a 1099 can be matched to the right recipient, not so this site becomes a place worth breaking into. The full number belongs on the signed W-9 in a locked drawer.
fields.label: Tax ID Last 4

fields.description: Mailing address, as it should be printed on a 1099.
fields.label: Address

fields.description: This party's row in the member register, when they hold an interest. The cap table already carries the legal name, so this link leaks nothing the register did not: it just stops the two drifting apart.
fields.label: Cap Table Entry

fields.description: This party as a vendor, when they are also paid. Linking them is what lets the 1099 pre-fill flag a recipient as a related party — which is a disclosure, not an error.
fields.label: Supplier

fields.description: The document that establishes this relationship: the operating agreement, the trust instrument, the appointment resolution.
fields.label: Governing Document

name: Related Party
